name: North Node Psychology
description: Defines psychological needs, sensitivities, protective strategies, regulation needs, blind spots, and integration markers for developmental practice.

coreNeed.definition: Enough psychological permission, time, and feedback to practice a less familiar complementary capacity without demanding immediate competence.

coreMotivation.definition: Increase the number of available responses by strengthening capacities that are not yet automatic or consolidated.

coreSensitivity.definition: Heightened awareness of discomfort, inefficiency, or uncertainty when using a less practiced mode.
Heightened awareness of the difference between existing competence and emerging ability.
Heightened awareness of others who appear more fluent in the emerging capacity.
Heightened awareness that the familiar South Node strategy is being used beyond the range where it remains adaptive.

coreFearPatterns.definition: Fear that temporary awkwardness proves inability or unsuitability.
Fear that developing the emerging capacity requires rejecting familiar strengths.
Fear that practice will expose weakness while reducing access to the established mode.
Fear of being seen while learning, experimenting, or performing below established standards.

protectiveStrategies.definition: Treat the emerging capacity as a perfected future identity rather than a practice.
Attempt to display mastery before sufficient repetition and feedback exist.
Reject or suppress familiar capacities in order to appear aligned with the emerging pole.
Return exclusively to the established pattern when the new mode feels inefficient or exposing.
Treat unfamiliarity as virtue and familiarity as failure.

blindSpots: Confusing rejection of the South Node with growth
Confusing temporary awkwardness with permanent incompetence
Underestimating the value of established strengths
Expecting development to feel immediately rewarding
Treating growth as a moral obligation

regulationNeeds.definition: Practice the emerging capacity in bounded situations where feedback is available.
Keep established skills available as support rather than treating them as forbidden.
Match the difficulty and exposure level to the current stage of practice.
Evaluate performance without converting it into a verdict about worth or destiny.
Assess whether the emerging capacity is broadening range rather than creating a new rigidity.

healthyPsychologicalFunctions: Use familiar strengths as developmental support
integrationMarkers: Can use the emerging capacity without performing an idealized identity
Can return to the South Node without shame
Can recognize when unfamiliarity is useful and when it is merely inefficient
Can practice publicly without demanding immediate competence
Can let feedback modify the developmental direction
Can coordinate both poles according to context
Can treat range expansion as an ongoing process
reflectionComponents: What would one small practice step look like?
Which South Node strength could support this practice?
What feedback would show that range is expanding?
Am I treating direction as destiny?
psychologyConstraints: No motive may be inferred from the North Node alone.
No developmental difficulty may be treated as pathology.
The South Node must remain available as a resource.
The North Node may not be described as moral superiority.
Developmental language must reference the global development blueprint.

provenance.sourcePolicy: Developmental-direction vocabulary only. Psychology and development qualify expression but do not convert the North Node into destiny, moral ranking, or guaranteed outcome.
